Three straight lines, 3 pixels wide, at 200 on a background of 60, 160 by 160 pixels, with Gaussian noise of sigma 20 from NumPy's default_rng with seed 7. The ridgelet rows use 180 angles, db4, 4 levels and hard thresholding. The Radon round trip alone, without noise, gives the clean lines back at only 29.32 dB, since the sampled transform blurs thin lines. That caps what any threshold can reach. Here ridgelet filtering beats the round trip but not wavelet thresholding.
